newsitem.title: CHINA: China earthquake leaves seven dead, 10 injured.
newsitem.headline: China earthquake leaves seven dead, 10 injured.

text.p: Two major earthquakes rocked China's westernmost Xinjiang region within one minute on Tuesday, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 10, officials said.

An earthquake measuring 6.4 on the open-ended Richter scale struck the Jiashi and Artux districts at 9.47 a.m. (0147 GMT), followed one minute later by a tremor measuring 6.3, an official of the State Seismological Bureau said.
"We are measuring this as a single earthquake of 6.4," he said.

However, an official of the seismological bureau in Jiashi said the stronger earthquake had measured at least 6.6 on the open-ended Richter scale, strong enough to cause widespread damage in the region, which is populated mainly by sheep herders.
At least seven people had been killed and 10 injured, he said, quoting initial reports for the Jiashi district, about 50 km (30 miles) from the mainly Moslem bazaar town of Kashgar.
The number of casualties could rise as rescue teams and officials searched through rubble of collapsed houses in the farming district around the town of Jiashi, the official said.

"We will know more later in the day as we get reports from outlying districts," he said by telephone, adding that local officials were checking the extent of damage in an area with a fairly large population of sheep farmers.

The earthquakes hit as most residents were on their way to work in a region where offices open officially at 10 a.m., because Beijing runs all of China as a single time zone despite actual time differences.
State television said an unknown number of houses in Jiashi had collapsed and cracks had appeared in many others.
"It felt much stronger than last time," the local official said, referring to an earthquake of 6.9 magnitude that rocked Jiashi in March last year, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
A special task force had been organised to check on damage throughout the district and to help with relief work, state television said.
A tremor measuring 5.0 on the open-ended Richter scale shook a remote corner of China's Tibet region on Monday.

The quake was centred in the Naqu region, about 600 km (360 miles) northwest of the regional capital, Lhasa. There were no immediate reports of injuries or damage and the mountainous region is thinly populated.
